title: Watch the 2026 Vanier Cup: Western Mustangs vs. Montréal Carabins

blocks.text: 2026 Vanier Cup: Montreal Carabins vs. Western Mustangs
Watch the Université de Montréal Carabins and the Western University Mustangs go head-to-head in the 61st edition of the prestigious Vanier Cup.

items: Montreal looks for rare repeat, Western in search of new winning era
'It's a privilege to play' in the Vanier Cup, Carabins coach Iadeluca says
Mustangs coach Faulds says ‘no moment is going to be too big’ for his team
Kickoff set for 12:07 p.m. ET at Quebec City’s Telus Stadium

November 28Adversity builds character — and Vanier Cup finalistsI spoke with both coaches in the build-up to the game, and each detailed a measure of adversity endured throughout their respective campaigns.Montreal dealt with a slew of injuries throughout the season, including the extended absence of star second-year quarterback Pepe Gonzalez, who suffered a collarbone injury in Week 5. Gonzalez returned in time to be a protagonist in the team’s Uteck Bowl win over UBC. The Carabins enter today’s game healthy and rejuvenated, with coach Iadeluca confirming Gonzalez is 100 per cent.Western, meanwhile, was handed an unfavourable Week 1 bye, meaning the team is set to become just the second school ever to play 13 games in as many weeks — joining Laval, which has done so on multiple occasions. Head coach Michael Faulds believes the extra game reps have afforded his young nucleus an opportunity to expedite its development en route to the title game.

MVP ready to do it all againJustin PiercyReigning Vanier Cup MVP Pepe Gonzalez aiming to lead Carabins to a 2nd-straight national titleCBC Sports' Arash Madani spoke with quarterback Pepe Gonzalez, as he looks to lead the Montreal Carabins to a second-straight Vanier Cup title on Saturday.There was no unknown quarterback at the helm of the Carabins this season. Pepe Gonzalez – the reigning Vanier Cup MVP – spoke with Arash Madani about how he’s aiming to lead Montreal to a second-straight national title.

Casselman flourished under centre (thanks to his mentor)Justin PiercyAfter taking over the Western Mustangs reins, QB Ben Casselman is ready for the Vanier Cup spotlightCBC Sports' Arash Madani spoke with Ben Casselman, who took over as the Western Mustangs starting quarterback midseason, and will be under centre in the Vanier Cup on Saturday.Ben Casselman wasn’t the starting quarterback for Western at the start of the season – but he spent the offseason training as if he was going to be. That preparation included spending part of the summer with one of the greatest Mustangs quarterbacks to ever do it. Arash Madani tells the story about how Casselman has thrived under the tutelage of Will Finch, who was the engine of a Western offence in the 2010s that came alive with the passing game.

Head coaches have their teams primedDion CaputiWestern Mustangs coach Faulds says 'no moment is going to be too big for this group'CBC Sports' Arash Madani spoke with Western Mustangs head coach Michael Faulds ahead of Saturday's Vanier Cup, against the reigning champion Montreal Carabins.I’m Dion Caputi, a producer with CBC Sports, and I’ll be sharing analysis throughout the game.Entering the 61st Vanier Cup, Montreal Carabins head coach Marco Iadeluca has the chance to become just the third man to win three Vanier Cups as a head coach — a feat only accomplished by Brian Towriss and Blake Nill. Iadeluca’s Carabins are the defending champions and will seek to win their third Vanier Cup since 2023.On the other end, Western head coach Michael Faulds left Laurier to return to his alma mater in January and has the Mustangs ahead of schedule after opening a new chapter, filling the shoes of his mentor Greg Marshall. Faulds has the blue-blood program ahead of schedule, marking its first return to the Vanier Cup since winning it in 2021.

Carabins' QB ready to goArash MadaniReigning Vanier Cup MVP Pepe Gonzalez getting loose before today's national championship game. Gonzalez had surgery less than two months ago (non-throwing shoulder) and returned for last week's Uteck Bowl. Told me he is able to make all the throws. Kickoff at noon ET, CBC https://t.co/v5PgZTnJY5—ArashMadani

Quebec City as permanent host?Today’s title game pits U Sports football’s past, represented by Western’s historic success, against its present, embodied by Montreal’s recent dominance. As for the future, it looks hazy – at least from a sports marketing standpoint.Morgan Campbell writes that on-field questions may centre on whether either team’s defence can slow down their opponent’s high-powered offence, but there’s also a more fundamental question about the Vanier Cup as a consumer product. Namely, how do you expand the game’s appeal beyond die-hard U Sports football followers, and make Canada’s national championship appointment viewing for everyday sports fans?This year, location solves part of that equation, but Campbell lays out why Telus Stadium isn’t a miracle cure in his story Quebec City is the ideal setting to try and catapult Vanier Cup back into relevance.

It's a Quebec City showdownJustin PiercyPowerhouse Showdown: Western Takes On Montreal in the Vanier CupCBC Sports' Arash Madani previews the 61st Vanier Cup. Tune in Saturday as the Western Mustangs and Montreal Carabins square off in the championship game.It’s been a chaotic post-season of U Sports football, full of upsets and new stars. Luckily for us, Arash Madani prepares us for today’s matchup between two powerhouse programs with the national title on the line.

It's game dayJustin PiercyGood morning, football fans! We’re just about an hour away from the start of the 61st edition of the Vanier Cup. Today, the defending champion Montreal Carabins take on the Western Mustangs for the right to be crowned U Sports football champions. Follow along for live updates and up-to-the minute analysis.
